_coverage.title: find_open_slots: the only source of times.

name: offers follow_up times for this friday using find_open_slots
input: Like any time after 1pm this Friday works.

conversation.content: Hi, I need to set up a follow-up at Elm Street.
Hi, this is Robin from Bramblewood Clinic. I can help with that. Can you please text me your full name and date of birth so I know I’m looking at the right chart?
Thanks, Jordan. Are you looking for an in-person follow-up or a telehealth video visit?
In-person, please. What do you have this Friday afternoon at Elm Street?

grading_criteria:
The assistant must:
- Understand the user is asking what times are available and must not make up or infer times.
- Call find_open_slots for a follow_up visit at Elm Street for this coming Friday afternoon, using a reasonable date range that includes that Friday.
- Offer only times that exactly match the slots returned by find_open_slots (slot_001, slot_002, slot_003). No extra fabricated times or altered times.
- Not imply that other times are available beyond those returned.
- Not attempt to book an appointment in this turn; it should first present 2–3 options and wait for the user to pick one, per the booking rule.
- Keep the reply short and friendly, no mention of tools.
The judge should confirm that every concrete time mentioned in the assistant reply corresponds to one of the find_open_slots results and that no time from the tool output is changed (e.g., rounded to 1:00 instead of 1:20).

checks.used_find_open_slots: Did the assistant call find_open_slots before offering any specific appointment times?
checks.no_fabricated_times: Did the assistant avoid inventing or modifying times that were not returned by find_open_slots?
checks.no_booking_yet: Did the assistant avoid calling book_appointment in this turn and instead just offer options for the user to choose from?
